title: The Life Maya Did Not Choose
title_ja: マヤが選ばなかった人生

source_links.title: Scientific background on counterfactual thinking and regret

fact_notes: マヤの事例は架空。反事実的思考・後悔については一般的な概念を扱い、特定の研究結果の再現を意図しない。

sentences.en: After graduating from secondary school, Maya looks back on a decision that once seemed minor: she declined an invitation to join a community research project.
sentences.ja: 高校を卒業した後、マヤは当時は小さく思えた決断、すなわち地域の調査活動への招待を断ったことを振り返ります。

sentences.en: At the time, she had been exhausted by examinations and believed that accepting another responsibility would leave too little time for rest.
sentences.ja: 当時は試験で疲れており、さらに責任を引き受けると休む時間がほとんどなくなると考えていました。

sentences.en: Several months later, she learns that the project introduced its participants to researchers and eventually received attention from a national educational organization.
sentences.ja: 数か月後、その活動が参加者に研究者と知り合う機会を与え、最終的に全国的な教育団体から注目されたと知ります。

sentences.en: Maya begins imagining an alternative life in which she accepted the invitation, met those researchers, and discovered an entirely different academic interest.
sentences.ja: マヤは招待を受け研究者と出会い、まったく別の学問的関心を見いだした別の人生を想像し始めます。

sentences.en: However, she notices that her imagined story contains successes but almost none of the problems that participating students might actually have encountered.
sentences.ja: しかし想像上の物語には成功が含まれる一方、参加した生徒たちが実際に直面したかもしれない問題はほとんどないと気づきます。

sentences.en: Her regret therefore raises a philosophical question about whether people can judge a past decision fairly by comparing reality with an alternative that never occurred.
sentences.ja: その後悔は、現実と実現しなかった別の選択を比べて過去の決断を公平に評価できるのかという哲学的な問いを生みます。

sentences.en: She also wonders whether learning an outcome makes the earlier choice appear more obviously mistaken than it could reasonably have seemed at the time.
sentences.ja: 結果を知ることで以前の選択が当時に比べて明らかに誤りだったように見えるのではないかとも考えます。

sentences.en: Instead of immediately labeling herself foolish, she decides to reconstruct what information and obligations were actually available when she made the choice.
sentences.ja: すぐ自分を愚かだったと決めつけず、選択時に実際どんな情報と責任があったか再構成することにします。

sentences.en: People sometimes imagine how their lives might have unfolded if they had chosen a different route, a process often described as counterfactual thinking.
sentences.ja: 人は別の道を選んでいたら人生がどう展開したか想像することがあり、しばしば反事実的思考と呼ばれます。

sentences.en: For example, a traveler who misses a train may picture arriving on time simply by imagining that the journey began five minutes earlier.
sentences.ja: 例えば電車に乗り遅れた旅人は出発を五分早めていれば間に合ったと想像するかもしれません。

sentences.en: Such comparisons can identify actions worth changing in the future, but they may also hide uncertainty about the alternative outcome.
sentences.ja: こうした比較は将来変えるべき行動を見つける一方で、別の結果についての不確かさを隠す場合もあります。

sentences.en: A person can usually describe the life that actually followed a decision more accurately than the many possible lives that did not happen.
sentences.ja: 人は通常、実際に選択の後をたどった人生は、起こらなかった数多くの可能な人生より正確に説明できます。

sentences.en: The imagined alternative therefore risks becoming unusually attractive because its difficulties do not have to be observed, measured, or remembered.
sentences.ja: したがって想像上の別の道は困難を観察・測定・記憶する必要がないため、異常に魅力的になり得ます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, dismissing all counterfactual reflection would ignore the way it can expose genuine mistakes or reveal opportunities for future improvement.
sentences.ja: それでも反事実的な振り返りをすべて退けると、本当の誤りを明らかにし将来の改善機会を見せる働きを無視することになります。

sentences.en: The important distinction is between using an imagined scenario as a question to investigate and treating it as an established account of what would certainly have happened.
sentences.ja: 重要な違いは想像した状況を調べるべき問いとして使うことと、確実に起きたはずの説明として扱うことです。

sentences.en: Maya begins to see her regret not as proof of failure but as evidence that she now values opportunities she previously underestimated.
sentences.ja: マヤは後悔を失敗の証明ではなく、以前は過小評価した機会を今では大切にしている証拠と考え始めます。

sentences.en: To evaluate her decision, Maya writes down the circumstances that existed before anyone knew how successful the research project would become.
sentences.ja: 決断を評価するためマヤは調査活動の成功を誰も知らなかった時点の事情を書き出します。

sentences.en: Her examination schedule was demanding, her family needed some help at home, and the project's workload had not been clearly explained.
sentences.ja: 試験日程は厳しく、家族は家庭での助けを必要とし、活動の仕事量は明確に説明されていませんでした。

sentences.en: Instead of comparing her actual decision with an imaginary path of guaranteed success, she asks what a thoughtful person could reasonably have concluded from those facts.
sentences.ja: 実際の決断を成功が保証された架空の道と比べず、慎重な人ならその事実から何を合理的に結論づけられたか尋ねます。

sentences.en: She realizes that the decision to protect her available time was not necessarily irresponsible, even if accepting the invitation might have brought valuable experiences.
sentences.ja: 招待を受ければ価値ある経験が得られたかもしれなくても、時間を守る決断は必ずしも無責任ではなかったと気づきます。

sentences.en: At the same time, she notices that she could have asked the organizers more questions before declining rather than deciding on the basis of incomplete information.
sentences.ja: 同時に、不完全な情報だけで断るより主催者にもっと質問できたはずだとも気づきます。

sentences.en: This observation provides a specific lesson that is more useful than the general accusation that she always chooses incorrectly.
sentences.ja: この観察は自分はいつも選択を間違えるという漠然とした非難より役立つ具体的な教訓を与えます。

sentences.en: It also preserves the difference between judging whether a decision was reasonable when made and judging whether its consequences later happened to be favorable.
sentences.ja: これは選択時の判断が合理的だったかと、その結果が後に好ましかったかの違いも保ちます。

sentences.en: A sound evaluation of past choices should take account of uncertainty as it existed then rather than pretending that later knowledge was always available.
sentences.ja: 過去の選択の適切な評価では後の知識が最初からあったかのように扱わず、当時の不確かさを考慮すべきです。

sentences.en: Maya discusses the problem with a classmate who participated in the project and learns that the experience was rewarding but also demanding.
sentences.ja: マヤは活動に参加した同級生と問題を話し合い、経験は有意義でしたが負担も大きかったと知ります。

sentences.en: The classmate describes friendships and opportunities, yet also remembers late meetings, disagreements, and periods of considerable pressure.
sentences.ja: 同級生は友情や機会を語る一方、遅い時間の会議や意見の相違、かなりの重圧が続く時期も覚えています。

sentences.en: Maya is careful not to turn this account into another simplistic story in which participation must have been either entirely good or entirely bad.
sentences.ja: マヤはこの説明を参加が完全によかったか悪かったかという別の単純な物語にしないよう気をつけます。

sentences.en: She recognizes that different participants could reasonably describe the same experience in different ways according to their responsibilities and expectations.
sentences.ja: 参加者によって責任や期待が異なり、同じ経験を合理的に違う形で説明できると認識します。

sentences.en: Moreover, she realizes that receiving a prestigious recognition does not automatically mean every individual participant benefited equally from the work.
sentences.ja: さらに名誉ある評価を受けたことは各参加者が活動から等しく利益を得たことを自動的に意味しないと気づきます。

sentences.en: The conversation helps her distinguish a project's public achievements from the private experiences of the people who contributed to it.
sentences.ja: この会話は活動の公の成果とそれに貢献した人々の個人的な経験を区別する助けとなります。

sentences.en: She is also reminded that another person's account deserves respect without being treated as a complete description of every possible outcome.
sentences.ja: 他者の説明を尊重しながらもあらゆる可能な結果の完全な説明とみなすべきではないと再認識します。

sentences.en: Her understanding becomes more complex, but the increased complexity makes her judgment less dependent on an attractive story she invented alone.
sentences.ja: 理解は複雑になりますが、その複雑さが自分一人で作った魅力的な物語への依存を減らします。

sentences.en: Several weeks later, Maya receives an invitation to help organize a smaller project at her university and notices the familiar feeling of uncertainty.
sentences.ja: 数週間後、マヤは大学で小さな活動の運営を手伝う招待を受け、以前と同じ不確かな気持ちに気づきます。

sentences.en: This time, she asks about the expected hours, the responsibilities involved, and the possibility of sharing tasks with other volunteers.
sentences.ja: 今回は必要な時間、関わる責任、ほかのボランティアと仕事を分担できるかについて尋ねます。

sentences.en: As a result, she has a clearer basis for deciding whether participation would fit alongside her academic and personal commitments.
sentences.ja: その結果、学業と個人的な責任に合うかを決めるためのより明確な根拠を得ます。

sentences.en: She eventually accepts a limited role, not because she can guarantee a successful outcome but because she understands the terms of the commitment.
sentences.ja: 最終的に限られた役割を引き受けますが、それは成功を保証できるからではなく責任の条件を理解したからです。

sentences.en: The decision does not erase her earlier regret, nor does it prove that accepting every new opportunity is wise.
sentences.ja: この決断は以前の後悔を消すわけでもすべての新しい機会を受けるのが賢明と証明するわけでもありません。

sentences.en: Instead, it demonstrates how reflection can improve the quality of later decisions without rewriting the facts of the past.
sentences.ja: むしろ過去の事実を書き換えずに振り返りが後の決断の質を改善できることを示します。

sentences.en: Maya comes to believe that the purpose of examining an imagined alternative is not to punish the person who once decided differently.
sentences.ja: マヤは想像上の別の道を考える目的は過去に異なる決断をした人を罰することではないと考えるようになります。

sentences.en: It is to ask more precise questions about responsibility, incomplete information, and the choices that remain possible in the present.
sentences.ja: 目的は責任、不完全な情報、現在なお可能な選択についてより正確な問いを立てることです。

questions.prompt: What weakness does Maya notice in her imagined alternative?
options: It follows the exact experiences of project members.
It is supported by a complete record of the past.
It includes successes while overlooking possible difficulties.
It contains no successful outcomes.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「しかし想像上の物語には成功が含まれる一方、参加した生徒たちが実際に直面したかもしれない問題はほとんどないと気づきます。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does Maya respond to her initial regret?
options: She destroys all accounts of the project.
She reconstructs the information and obligations available at the time.
She decides that every missed opportunity proves failure.
She blames the project participants.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「すぐ自分を愚かだったと決めつけず、選択時に実際どんな情報と責任があったか再構成することにします。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is a possible benefit and risk of counterfactual comparisons?
options: They can suggest improvements while hiding uncertainty about alternatives.
They always reveal exactly what would have happened.
They never influence future decisions.
They prove every earlier decision was unreasonable.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「こうした比較は将来変えるべき行動を見つける一方で、別の結果についての不確かさを隠す場合もあります。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What key distinction does the passage draw?
options: Choosing a preferred story and treating it as history.
Rejecting every form of reflection.
Replacing real events with fictional memories.
Treating imagined outcomes as questions rather than established facts.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「重要な違いは想像した状況を調べるべき問いとして使うことと、確実に起きたはずの説明として扱うことです。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does Maya use instead of a guaranteed-success comparison?
options: The opinions of people she has never met.
A list of future events presented as known.
The facts that were available when the original choice was made.
Only the project's later public recognition.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「実際の決断を成功が保証された架空の道と比べず、慎重な人ならその事実から何を合理的に結論づけられたか尋ねます。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What specific improvement does she identify?
options: Ignoring the project's workload.
Asking organizers more questions before making a decision.
Always accepting new projects.
Avoiding every difficult responsibility.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「同時に、不完全な情報だけで断るより主催者にもっと質問できたはずだとも気づきます。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the project's public recognition fail to guarantee?
options: That every participant benefited equally.
That the project received attention.
That people worked on the project.
That the organizers completed activities.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「さらに名誉ある評価を受けたことは各参加者が活動から等しく利益を得たことを自動的に意味しないと気づきます。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does hearing a participant's account affect Maya?
options: It proves her own choice was entirely wrong.
It eliminates all uncertainty about alternative lives.
It convinces her that personal accounts are useless.
It makes her evaluation more nuanced and less dependent on her imagined story.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「理解は複雑になりますが、その複雑さが自分一人で作った魅力的な物語への依存を減らします。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why does Maya accept a limited role in a later project?
options: The project cannot involve any problems.
Her earlier regret has completely disappeared.
She understands the commitment, not because success is guaranteed.
She has learned to accept every invitation.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「最終的に限られた役割を引き受けますが、それは成功を保証できるからではなく責任の条件を理解したからです。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: Which claim best captures the main argument?
options: Regret should always be avoided by refusing new responsibilities.
Counterfactual reflection is most useful when it improves future judgment without pretending to know an unrealized past.
Imagined alternatives show exactly which past choices were mistakes.
Good decisions can be evaluated only by later public success.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「目的は責任、不完全な情報、現在なお可能な選択についてより正確な問いを立てることです。」が正答の根拠です。

paraphrases.source: Instead of immediately labeling herself foolish, she decides to reconstruct what information and obligations were actually available when she made the choice.
paraphrases.rewrite: Maya examines what could reasonably have been known when she refused the opportunity.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 過去の時点で知り得た情報を検討します。

paraphrases.source: The important distinction is between using an imagined scenario as a question to investigate and treating it as an established account of what would certainly have happened.
paraphrases.rewrite: Imagined scenarios should be treated as questions, not as certain histories.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 想像は確実な歴史として扱いません。

paraphrases.source: A sound evaluation of past choices should take account of uncertainty as it existed then rather than pretending that later knowledge was always available.
paraphrases.rewrite: Fair evaluation of an old decision must consider uncertainty that existed at that moment.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 当時の不確かさを考慮します。

paraphrases.source: It is to ask more precise questions about responsibility, incomplete information, and the choices that remain possible in the present.
paraphrases.rewrite: Reflection should improve present choices rather than condemn the past through imagined certainty.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 現在の選択改善が目的という結論です。
